syllabus.clause: point reads/writes vs large scans and aggregates; normalization pressure, row vs column layout and indexing, and why one schema rarely serves both.

at.step: Reveal: row storage reads whole rows regardless
Reveal: normalization pressure pulls the other way for each

items.item: Row-wise storage stores an entire record's values together per block; OLTP applications typically read or write entire records, so row-wise storage is optimal for them

at.step: Reveal: row storage reads whole rows regardless

items.item: Columnar storage stores each column's values together; a query over five of a hundred columns reads about five percent of the table, versus a row-wise database reading the other ninety-five columns' blocks too
OLTP's normalization splits data into smaller, less redundant tables so independent transactions can be processed without colliding

at.step: Reveal: normalization pressure pulls the other way for each

items.item: Querying highly normalized data for analytics needs joins to denormalize it, and aggregate queries over many transactions are resource-intensive for an OLTP system

at.step: Reveal: normalization pressure pulls the other way for each
